reason: The text explicitly portrays Samuel as a young servant (נַעַר, na'ar—a non-leader) who possesses and exercises significant agency throughout the passage. Samuel responds to God's calls, makes decisions (e.g., returning to sleep, later speaking with Eli), receives and delivers divine messages, and his words carry power ('not one of his words fell to the ground'). Additionally, the community demonstrates collective agency when 'the elders of Israel said' (זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) and decided to bring the Ark. The text directly contradicts the premise by showing that non-leaders like Samuel and the assembled people both possess and exercise meaningful agency.
